\begin{abstract}
We combine three restricted mechanisms developed after the frustrated-boundary
obstruction: conditional concentration under coherent staples, exact charging
of center frustration, and a dependent Gaussian bad-set theorem.  For each
connected plaquette support $X$, split the nonlinear bad event according to a
coherent-collar event $G_X$.  If the good channel costs at most a
Radon--Nikodym factor $e^{\kappa|X|}$ relative to the Gaussian rate $J$, and
the collar-failure channel costs $e^{-K|X|}$, then the complete connected-event
envelope has weight $q_{\rm eff}=e^{\kappa-J}+e^{-K}$.  We prove the resulting rooted
event criterion and calculate the exact remaining budget at the frozen
ultraviolet witness.  The abstract transfer closes for $\kappa=0.2$ and
$K=7.0$; proving those inequalities for the complete nonlinear
$\mathrm{SU}(2)$ measure remains open.
\end{abstract}

\tableofcontents

\section{Two channels and their information content}

Let $B_X$ denote the event that every plaquette in a connected support $X$ is
bad at radius $\rho$.  Let $G_X$ be the gauge-covariant coherent-collar event
defined from the surrounding staple family.  The decomposition
\[
 B_X=(B_X\cap G_X)\mathbin{\dot\cup}(B_X\cap G_X^c)
\]
retains the distinction erased by arbitrary microscopic conditioning.

The dependent Gaussian theorem supplies a per-plaquette rate $J$.  The two
nonlinear proof obligations are
\begin{equation}
 \mu(B_X\cap G_X)\leq e^{\kappa|X|}e^{-J|X|}.
 \label{eq:good}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \mu(B_X\cap G_X^c)\leq e^{-K|X|}.
 \label{eq:collar}
\end{equation}
The first measures nonlinear action, Haar, and coordinate comparison on a good
collar.  The second charges the cause of collar failure, including center and
topological labels, to the same support.

\section{Transfer theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Two-tier connected-event envelope]
If \eqref{eq:good}--\eqref{eq:collar} hold for every connected $X$, then
\begin{equation}
 \mu(B_X)\leq q_{\rm eff}^{|X|},
 \qquad
 q_{\rm eff}=e^{\kappa-J}+e^{-K}.
 \label{eq:qeff}
\end{equation}
If the plaquette adjacency degree is at most $\Delta$ and
\begin{equation}
 e^\alpha\Delta^2q_{\rm eff}<1,
 \label{eq:criterion}
\end{equation}
then
\begin{equation}
 \sup_p\sum_{\substack{X\ni p\\ X\ \mathrm{connected}}}
 e^{\alpha|X|}\mu(B_X)
 \leq
 \frac{e^\alpha q_{\rm eff}}
 {1-e^\alpha\Delta^2q_{\rm eff}}.
 \label{eq:rooted}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The disjoint split and \eqref{eq:good}--\eqref{eq:collar} give
\[
 \mu(B_X)\leq a^{|X|}+b^{|X|}
 \leq(a+b)^{|X|},
 \qquad a=e^{\kappa-J},\quad b=e^{-K},
\]
which proves \eqref{eq:qeff}.  Bound the number of rooted connected sets of
size $n$ by $\Delta^{2(n-1)}$ and sum the geometric series.  This gives
\eqref{eq:rooted} under \eqref{eq:criterion}.
\end{proof}

The critical effective weight is
\begin{equation}
 q_{\rm crit}=\frac{e^{-\alpha}}{\Delta^2}.
 \label{eq:qcrit}
\end{equation}
If collar failure were absent, the maximum comparison loss permitted by the
counting criterion would be
\begin{equation}
 \kappa_{\max}=J+\log q_{\rm crit}.
 \label{eq:kmax}
\end{equation}
At fixed $\kappa$ with $e^{\kappa-J}<q_{\rm crit}$, the collar rate must obey
\begin{equation}
 K> -\log\bigl(q_{\rm crit}-e^{\kappa-J}\bigr).
 \label{eq:kmin}
\end{equation}

\section{Frozen nonlinear budget}

Insert the dependent Gaussian rate $J=6.69010106986$, $\alpha=0.1$, and
$\Delta=18$.  For the declared targets $\kappa=0.2$ and $K=7.0$:
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}lr@{}}
\toprule
quantity & value\\
\midrule
good-channel weight $e^{\kappa-J}$ & $0.00151839554$\\
collar weight $e^{-K}$ & $0.000911881966$\\
$q_{\rm eff}$ & $0.00243027750$\\
$q_{\rm crit}$ & $0.00279270808$\\
weight slack & $0.000362430579$\\
branching ratio & $0.870222534$\\
rooted sum upper & $0.0206959813$\\
$\kappa_{\max}$ without collar failure & $0.809357554$\\
minimum $K$ at $\kappa=0.2$ & $6.66534843$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Thus the declared pair is strictly sufficient for this counting theorem.  It
is a target budget, not a measured or proved property of the nonlinear link
measure.

\section{Finite multiscale composition}

At scales $j=1,\ldots,N$, define
\[
 q_j=e^{\kappa_j-J_j}+e^{-K_j},
 \qquad r_j=e^{\alpha_j}\Delta_j^2q_j.
\]
If every $r_j<1$, then the declared finite-registry exceptional error is
bounded by
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{j=1}^N\frac{e^{\alpha_j}q_j}{1-r_j}.
 \label{eq:multiscale}
\end{equation}
For the four-scale illustrative registry in the executable calibration, this
sum is $0.0286463$.  Equation \eqref{eq:multiscale} is a composition lemma.  It
does not construct RG maps, prove that the registry follows the Yang--Mills
flow, or establish infinite-scale summability.

\section{Exact next theorem and frontier audit}

The first unproved analytic implication has become the following pair of inequalities,
for the complete finite-volume heat-kernel $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ measure, uniformly
in volume and admitted exterior gauge-invariant data:
\begin{align*}
 \mu(B_X\cap G_X)&\leq e^{0.2|X|}\mu_{\rm G}(B_X^{\rm lin}),\\
 \mu(B_X\cap G_X^c)&\leq e^{-7|X|}.
\end{align*}
They must use the same $t$, $\rho$, $\eta$, block geometry, and support.  The
collar channel must retain center flux, boundary holonomy, orbit-atlas failure,
and topology rather than optimizing them away.

The theorem bounds connected bad events.  To obtain a partition-function
cluster expansion, one must additionally construct the relevant nonlinear
polymers or prove a stochastic domination theorem that legitimately uses this
event envelope.  No Mayer/Ursell activity identification is asserted here.

The transfer theorem and its budget are C2 results.  Nonlinear full-measure
control, repeated RG, continuum coherence, Osterwalder--Schrader
reconstruction, and the mass gap remain open.
